title: Soviet missiles brought online

plain: In the 1960s, Soviet nuclear missiles were reportedly switched on, or "brought online", by something unexplained. A guest named Karl Nell, who speaks from an official background, tells Michels this was "an analogous thing" to similar incidents with American missiles. He says documents and testimony show it was real. He credits records released under FOIA, a US law that lets anyone request government records. If true, the same unexplained interference with nuclear weapons happened on both sides of the Cold War.
